descriptionChirho: To open wide, especially the mouth or jaws, either literally or as a gesture of hostility or astonishment; the basic physical meaning of patsah referring to gaping or spreading open.

To open the mouth for the purpose of speaking or uttering words, emphasizing verbal expression rather than mere physical opening; attested by Arabic nataqat (uttered) and Swahili zilisema (they spoke).
To rescue, deliver, or snatch away from danger or oppression; an extended or metaphorical sense of patsah meaning to open or break free, used in contexts of divine or human deliverance.
